supplementary_observations.observation: Under “Planned relation outcome (helper observe → plan),” it labels the commit-only keyword consequence a “pr-keyword-removal / Git-owner handoff” and predicts needs-input. The frozen command interface observes entity bodies and Development provenance, not commit messages; it does not establish that this commit-only risk will produce that helper handoff. The semantic Git-owner handoff and merge hold are correct, so the frozen criteria pass.

It says “The plan should emit a closing-intent decision and a keyword-removal handoff for the commit keyword.” The frozen helper interface carries entity bodies and Development provenance without commit-message observation, so that mechanical handoff claim is unsupported for the fixture’s commit-only keyword and missing edge. The response correctly retains a separate owner decision and holds merge; this is supplementary, not a frozen-rubric failure.

The proposed observe request explicitly has no body_edits, but the response predicts no body-authoring handoffs because the existing entries are accurate. Frozen references/command.md says missing body decisions produce authoring handoffs and the command does not parse Markdown or infer ledger boundaries. Retain-unchanged writer decisions are needed to substantiate that mechanical no-handoff prediction. This implementation-shape claim does not undermine the three frozen semantic criteria.

It predicts a ready plan with no Issue-writer or PR-writer handoff solely because existing ledger entries are accurate, without carrying writer-owned unchanged-body decisions. Frozen references/command.md states that missing body decisions produce authoring handoffs and that the helper does not parse Markdown or infer boundaries. The intended no-byte-change and authorized-only unlink behavior satisfies the frozen criteria; the mechanical no-handoff prediction needs an explicit unchanged decision.

It says the operator’s supplied observation satisfies reacquisition and therefore there should be no setting_requests, while also requiring its original timestamp to be later than the invalidation boundary. The frozen interface records that boundary when the event is first seen, and the fixture supplies no qualifying timestamp; helper selection must decide whether a further single acquisition is needed. This overstates acceptance of the supplied observation. The stale plan remains invalidated and the unsafe partial add remains blocked, so the frozen criteria pass.

This is too narrow for continuation handling; the response still retains stored artifacts and no pending body work is known to have been lost.

supplementary_observations.observation: The response predicts that helper observe/plan will produce a 'pr-keyword-removal-class handoff' for a keyword in a commit. The frozen command interface's pr-keyword-removal handoff is a PR-content route; commit messages remain outside the helper's supported surface and their unresolved consequences belong to the Git owner. The response chooses that owner correctly, so the exact relation expectations pass, but it should not invent a helper-produced PR-content handoff for commit text.

The ordered workflow invokes writing-reviewable-pr-descriptions for body-only candidates in step 4, then chooses review mode and specialists in step 5. The integrated writer/publisher instructions require the explicit mode and sorted specialist inventory before invoking the writer or freezing the candidate. This is a concrete sequencing mismatch in the PR105 instruction surface, separate from the four declared relation expectations, which pass.

The ordered fixup workflow hands authoring to the PR writer in step 4 with only diff and relation intent, then adds explicit review mode/specialists at creation in step 5. Its unresolved gate says mode selection blocks creation, not writer invocation. The integrated writer/publisher instructions require that selection before invoking the writer. The four declared relation expectations still pass.

The ordered authoring handoff does not bind publication-review mode or specialists, and the gate says they need selection only before the writer freezes the candidate. The integrated instructions require the selected mode and sorted inventory before the writer is invoked, so this states a weaker boundary than the new contract. The four declared relation expectations still pass.
